title: Compliant Amazon Main Images at Scale | AIVideosUGC
description: Follow Amazon's product image requirements with one compliant white main image. Use that setup at scale, then send every backpack to Seller Central.
h1: Amazon Product Image Requirements for Every Listing
lead: Give every olive canvas backpack the same pure-white main image, then send the set to Seller Central. Keep the sale badge off this picture, and put the pack you ship large in the square.
summary: One white setup covers the whole backpack catalog, not just the first color. The square stays white, the product stays large, and the frame stays limited to what the box contains.

sections.h2: One White Main Image for Every Backpack
paras: Give every olive canvas backpack the same pure-white main image, then send that set to Seller Central. Sale stickers, badges, and extra objects stay off this picture.

Start with the corners of that backpack square. Amazon wants those corners at 255 on red, green, and blue. The backpack should fill most of the square. The product in the frame should be the one you ship, straps included when the straps ship, with no text drawn on. Small lettering on a label should still be readable when you zoom. When the square matches the backpack in your hand, you can publish that file as the main image. Later pictures can show the pack in use. This first picture stays the clean white one.

paras: A shop with thirty backpacks can reuse the white square once the first pack looks right. Save that setup and apply it to pack thirty.
A clean main image can also be the first picture on your own store.
You set pure white once, choose how much of the square the backpack fills, and name what ships in the box. The next product uses that setup.
You confirm shape, color, straps, and label against the backpack in your hand, and then you publish the file that matches.

sections.h2: Start From a Phone Photo, Not a Studio
paras: You do not need a white studio. The phone photo needs the whole backpack, sharp, with even light and a little space around every edge.

Take the photo near a window, on a plain surface, and hold the phone at the backpack's height. Show what the buyer finds in the box, including both straps. Leave a little empty space around the pack so the edges are not cut off. Flash on a canvas weave can blow out the color, so window light is safer.

sections.h2: Make the Pure White Main Image
paras: The olive canvas backpack, straps included, is already in the phone photo, and that is the group you ask for on white.

Open the [AI product background changer](page:change-background) or the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub). Type one plain line, such as the olive canvas backpack and both straps on pure white, filling most of the square. Then sample a corner. It should read 255 on red, green, and blue.

sections.h2: Use the Same White Setup on Every SKU
paras: A white main image keeps a backpack listing easy to find in search. Replace a gray main image and the listing can show in search again. The later photos are not the ones this rule is about.

Once the first backpack's square is right, use that same square on the next color. The API is not a separate install. It can start the job from the catalog you already keep, so a new color uses the setup you already checked.

sections.h2: Keep One Look on the Later Images
paras: Save the shop's navy and the wordmark for the photos after the main image. Those later photos are where colors and the wordmark belong. The main image stays a clean product on white, with no lettering.

The white square is only the first picture. The backpack on a chair, or a hand on the strap for scale, belongs in the later spots. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) and [photos with a person](page:model-photos) cover those spots. Do not move the wordmark onto the main image.

sections.h2: How to Make Amazon Listing Photos in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Upload your product photo. Get the main image right on one backpack before you touch the rest. The square is white, and the straps are in it when the straps ship.

Describe your scene for the later pictures. The second picture can be the backpack on a chair. Add your navy caption in the editor only on that later image. Match the long side to the size your category currently asks for.
Download and post. When that pair looks right, repeat it for the other backpacks and send the files to Seller Central. Upload the white file you already checked.

sections.h2: Check the Backpack Before You Upload
paras: You upload a file whose corners are full white and whose backpack matches the one in your hand. Check the corners with a color picker, then set the real pack next to the screen and compare the straps, the color, and the label.

Each corner should be pure white, with no gray haze. Zoom in on labels, because small lettering is where a new image often goes wrong. If the words are wrong, try again from a sharper phone photo before the file goes to Seller Central.
sections.alt: Adult hands compare an olive canvas backpack with a blank white square card.

sections.h2: When the Product Is White, Clear, or a Set
paras: Set the backpack's shape first, light the edges, and show exactly how many pieces the listing sells.

Side light keeps a pale product's outline visible on white. Take the starting photo with light from one side, so the outline has soft shading, and mention that side light in the line you type. If two straps ship, both straps stay in the frame. A clear bottle in the same catalog needs the same edge light, or it can disappear into the white.
sections.alt: Adult hand shapes an olive canvas backpack upright on a white backdrop.

sections.h2: Keep White for the Main Image Only
paras: Only the first picture has to be the white square. Picture two can show the backpack on a chair. Picture three can show the strap up close.

A useful set might show the backpack in a hallway, a hand for size, and a close view of the buckle. Make the pictures first, then add any words in the editor. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) are for those later spots. A soft shadow, when you want one, stays off the main image.

sections.h2: Upload the White Square You Checked
paras: A large backpack, white corners, the right straps, and a readable label are the file you upload. Check the pack in your hand against that file.

faq.q: What does Amazon want on the main image?
faq.a: The backpack you ship, large in the square, on white that reads 255 on red, green, and blue. A sticker, a badge, or an extra object stays off this picture. The product should fill most of the frame.

faq.q: What happens if the main image breaks the rules?
faq.a: The listing can drop out of search until you replace that main image with a compliant square. A photo of the backpack on a chair belongs in a later spot, not in the main square.

faq.q: How do I get a pure white background from a phone photo?
faq.a: Start from a phone photo that already shows the whole backpack. Ask for white, then sample a corner. A corner that is not 255 on red, green, and blue is not done yet.

faq.q: Can I do this for many backpacks together?
faq.a: Yes. After the first backpack is right, the next colors can use that same square. Each color keeps that product's own straps, color, and label.

faq.q: Can my shop system start the white image?
faq.a: Yes. If your shop system already lists every item, it can send the photo and ask for the white square in a batch. You still compare each file with the product in your hand.

faq.q: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?
faq.a: The corners are not full white. Check them with a color picker and ask for RGB 255, 255, 255 again. A gray haze at the edge is enough for the square to fail.

faq.q: Can an image made here be my Amazon main image?
faq.a: Yes, if it shows the real backpack, on pure white, with nothing extra drawn on. Compare it with the pack you ship before you upload it to Seller Central.

faq.q: How many credits does one white image use?
faq.a: 24 credits. The cost shows before the job starts. If it does not finish, those credits come back. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
It keeps the shape in the photo you uploaded. If a strap, a buckle, or the label shifts, try again from a sharper photo before you publish the file.

faq.q: What if the product is white, clear, or a set?
faq.a: Light it from the side so the edge still reads, and keep every piece that ships in the frame. A pale pack on white needs that edge or it can disappear.
